lines.text: Do you know how a nuclear power plant works? Inside, there's no fire at all. And yet it can power a whole city.
It starts with uranium fuel pellets, each about the size of a fingertip. One pellet holds roughly as much energy as a tonne of coal.
When a neutron hits a uranium atom, the atom splits in two. That releases heat, plus two or three new neutrons.
Those neutrons split more atoms, which release even more neutrons. A chain reaction.
To keep it steady, control rods sit between the fuel. They soak up neutrons. Push them in, and the reaction slows down.
All that heat turns water into high pressure steam.
The steam spins a giant turbine, which turns a generator. And that's your electricity.
And those huge towers? They cool the water back down. What rises from the top is water vapor, not smoke.
So in the end, nuclear power is a very clever way to boil water.
